items.title: Klopp begraaft strijdbijl met Nagelsmann na gevoelige uitspraken
items.summary: Tijdens het teleurstellende WK van Duitsland onder leiding van Julian Nagelsmann deed Jürgen Klopp een uitspraak die veel stof deed opwaaien in het land. 'Gelukkig stelt Nagelsmann nog het team samen', zei Klopp na het WK-duel met Curaçao, waarna hij na een korte stilte ongelukkig toevoegde: 'Nog steeds.' Er was destijds al veel speculatie rondom de voormalig Liverpool-manager om Nagelsmann op te volgen, wat op vrijdag bevestigd is . Klopp heeft meermaals zijn excuses aangeboden en wilde op zijn eerste persconferentie als bondscoach nog maar eens benadrukken dat de strijdbijl begraven is.

items.title: Football Daily | Manchester United and the quest to make mythical midfield a reality
items.summary: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Like the urban myth that you are never more than three feet away from a spider, modern footballing lore tells us Manchester United are only ever three signings away from a Premier League title challenge. With the Geopolitics World Cup in the rear-view mirror and the transfer news machine churning once more, you may have missed United being linked with just about every midfielder to ever grace a centre circle. They missed out on Elliot Anderson – who went and dubbed his new club the “kings of Manchester” – and were fooled into thinking they could snare Aurélien Tchouaméni. They danced briefly with Atalanta’s Éderson, before landing on Chelsea resale project prospect Andrey Santos and former Aston Villa linchpin Youri Tielemans. And United aren’t done with their midfield overhaul – rightly so given they have lost Casemiro to Inter Miami and Manuel Ugarte to long-term knee knack. Next up on United’s extensive longlist: Real Madrid’s Eduardo Camavinga and Fulham’s Sander Berge, plus France GWC sensation Manu Koné as Michael Carrick eyes the final piece in his midfield puzzle. items.title: Jürgen Klopp vows to change Germany but threatens to quit if family hounded by media
items.summary: Suggests role will be his final job in top-level football Warns journalists to ‘leave my family in peace’ Jürgen Klopp said he wants his team to “change a country” after being confirmed as Germany’s new head coach, but threatened to stand down if his family are hounded by the media during his time in charge. In a forthright first press conference upon his unveiling as Julian Nagelsmann’s replacement, Klopp also suggested the role will be his final job in top-level football and expressed regret after poking fun at his predecessor while working as a television pundit during the World Cup. He is tasked with reviving Germany, who lost to Paraguay in the last 32 and have not made the last 16 since winning the tournament in 2014. Continue reading...
